note: CATALOG-03 candidates (Issue #28): four user-selected repositories. Metadata only: every field is the publisher's own description read from the pinned commit, never a review, a test or an authorisation; the publishers' instructions (including pipe-to-shell installers) were read as data and are recorded only as labels. Each `record` conforms to schemas/catalog-entry.schema.json v2. `entryKind`, `pluginIdentity`, `sourcePath`, `purpose` and `executionPolicy` are application-level wrapper fields, as in the earlier candidate files.

notes: High privacy impact: it records what the agent does (commands, file contents, project details) and summarises it with a model, so secrets that appear in a session can be stored and sent to whichever provider is configured. A private-tag mechanism exists to exclude content; whether it is sufficient was not reviewed.

Local storage (SQLite and a vector index) and hosted options are different things. The README names a hosted memory service as the default for one integration path (Grok Bot), a hosted observer with a free trial after sign-in, and cloud backup; none of that may be assumed for other clients, and none was reviewed. Retention, deletion and provider data handling are unreviewed.

Quarantined and blocked until a scoped review of data flow, hooks, storage, retention and provider handling. This record starts no storage, worker or hook. Overlaps in purpose with a per-session memory the user may already use; see docs/catalog-03/RISK_AND_OVERLAP.md.

The README also contains a section about a third-party token named CMEM; it was not evaluated and is irrelevant to this catalog. Telemetry is not stated in the README, so it is unknown (the repository root holds a report file whose name mentions an analytics product; it was not opened).

notes: This single repository is a multi-module harness: the marketplace manifest lists 47 separate plugin modules (core, console, mods, swarm, browser, security, federation and more). It is one catalog candidate here, not 'all modules installed'; each module would need its own review.

Packaging identity is ambiguous: the root package.json is named claude-flow (3.61.1) and the plugin manifest is a stale claude-flow 2.5.0 that points at another repository and at 'alpha' and 'latest' npm tags, while the README offers 'ruflo'. Nothing here concludes that they are the same package.

High runtime privilege: hooks, a daemon, autonomous loops, workspace files, delegated agents, resource use and optional remote communication can change how the user works. Quarantined and blocked until a scoped review; no hook, daemon or file is created by this record.

Conflicts to expect with the application's own future agent-orchestration and control model, with workflow methods such as superpowers, and with memory plugins such as claude-mem (two hook systems rewriting the same session).
